contexts.text: Such ferocity of disposition exists in a great part of soldiers and their commanders. Described. SE 1063.
Where the good of love is, there the Lord fights for it, that is, for those who are in it. Signified.
Jehovah shall fight for you () = that the Lord alone endures the combats of temptations. Explained. AC 8219.
That the soldiers did this, () = that it was done by those who ought to have fought for truths...

That good loves truth, may be illustrated by... a soldier. If he is in the love of warfare, and feels good in protection or fame, he, from this good and according to it, acquires its knowledge; and, if he is a commander, its intelligence...
Therefore (jealousy) is seated in commanders of soldiers more than in others.
(Therefore) it is glorious for a soldier to shed his blood for his country.
Like a common soldier under his officer.

It is different with those who (kill and spoil) from duty, because they think of them as enemies; thus from orders; some of whom I have met who are among the more blessed, although soldiers. It is the interiors which condemn (there).
Soldiers, in special (glory in their potency).

They who altogether deny the Lord... are meant also by the soldier who pierced His side (). By the soldier, and the soldiers there, are meant those who are of the Church, and who ought to fight for the Lord; in special, those of the Jewish Church; and, in general, all who being of the Church are in falsities and evils. As the soldiers = these, they divided His garments. Explained. AE 64:4. AE 64:end. AE 195:21.
The soldiers () = those who should fight for the truths and goods of the Church.
That He fights as a hero and a man of war in battles. Illustrated.
Falsities of evil fighting against the goods of the Church, are signified by the multitude of all the nations which fight against Mount Zion ().
To fight upon Mount Zion, and upon its hill () = to do Judgment from Divine truth.

Charity in the common soldier. - If he looks to the Lord, and shuns evils as sins, and does his work sincerely, justly, and faithfully, he also becomes a charity... He is averse to unjust depredation; he abominates the wrongful effusion of blood. Otherwise in battles: he is then not averse to it, because he then does not think about it; but about the enemy as an enemy, who wants his blood. His fury ceases when he hears the sound of the drum calling him to desist from slaughter. He looks upon his captives after victory as the neighbour, according to the quality of their good. Before battle he raises his mind to the Lord, and commends his life into His hand; and, after he has done this, he lets his mind down from its elevation into the body, and becomes brave; the thought of the Lord, which he is then unconscious of, remaining still in his mind, above his bravery. And then, if he dies, he dies in the Lord; if he lives, he lives in the Lord.
